definition: Tech mining or technology mining refers to applying text mining methods to technical documents.
details: For patent analysis purposes, it is named ‘patent mining’. Porter, as one of the pioneers in technology mining, defined ‘tech mining’ in his book as follows: “the application of text mining tools to science and technology information, informed by understanding of technological innovation processes.” Therefore, tech mining has two significant characteristics: 1) using ‘text mining tools’, 2) applying these tools to ‘technology management’. Also, technology mining can be considered as one of technology intelligence branches.

explainer.lead: Technology mining, or tech mining, applies text mining methods to technical documents, especially for patent analysis. It matters for technology management and innovation analysis.

tiers.eli5: Using computer programs to read lots of technical or patent documents and find useful patterns, like what new technologies are emerging.
tiers.practitioner: Analysts apply text mining tools to science and technology information to inform technology management, often called patent mining when focused on patents. A pitfall is that results depend on document quality and domain-specific preprocessing.
tiers.paperLevel: Porter defined tech mining as the application of text mining tools to science and technology information, informed by understanding of technological innovation processes. It has two significant characteristics: using text mining tools and applying them to technology management.

explainer.example: Scanning thousands of patent abstracts to identify emerging clusters of technologies in a field.
